# Odette Pullen

## Overview

- **Gender:** female  <sub>[v1 c6 P4](../source/v01-c06.md#nw-v01-c06-p0004), [v1 c15 P76](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0076), [v1 c26 P21](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0021)</sub>
- **Role:** schoolteacher  <sub>[v1 c30 P21](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0021), [v1 c36 P24](../source/v01-c36.md#nw-v01-c36-p0024), [v1 c37 P34](../source/v01-c37.md#nw-v01-c37-p0034), [v2 c4 P0](../source/v02-c04.md#nw-v02-c04-p0000)</sub>

## Appearance

Odette wears a ribbon in the Regent's colors—scarlet and purple—pinned to her coat during her time at Regent's Academy. She is considered by Isolde and Nell to be a very nice, sensible, and ladylike girl.

_Sources: [v1 c34 P20](../source/v01-c34.md#nw-v01-c34-p0020), [v2 c26 P59](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0059)_

## Personality

Odette is steady, hardworking, dutiful, and remarkably composed, remaining unshakeable even during nerve-wracking exams. She is deeply practical and sensible, devoid of grand or ungrounded aspirations, aiming simply to earn her pay, satisfy the school board, and fulfill her duties. In classroom discipline, she takes a pragmatic approach and is willing to administer thrashings to keep order. She feels foolish writing about romance or reading it aloud, preferring realistic, down-to-earth stories.

_Sources: [v1 c26 P21](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0021), [v1 c31 P30](../source/v01-c31.md#nw-v01-c31-p0030), [v1 c32 P18](../source/v01-c32.md#nw-v01-c32-p0018), [v1 c35 P6](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0006), [v1 c36 P0](../source/v01-c36.md#nw-v01-c36-p0000), [v2 c4 P2](../source/v02-c04.md#nw-v02-c04-p0002), [v2 c4 P6](../source/v02-c04.md#nw-v02-c04-p0006), [v2 c26 P59](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0059)_

## History

Odette grew up in Brierley and attended the local school under Mr. Pidgeon, nearly drowning during a trip to the Lake of Glassy Waters before being saved by her father. She became a close companion of Nell Harcourt, Isolde Pembroke, and Opal Pettigrew, participating in school recitations, playing Queen Guinevere in an outdoor enactment of Lancelot and Elaine, and joining the girls' weekly tale-writing society. Following her studies under Miss Thorne, Odette entered the Regent's class to prepare for the Entrance exam, intending to become a teacher to earn her own independent income. She passed the exams smoothly and achieved top marks in domestic science at Regent's Academy. After graduating, Odette accepted a teaching position in Stonebridge, where she became highly liked and gained a place on the Inspector's Honor Roll. She actively supported the Brierley Village Improvement Society by collecting door-to-door funds and serving on committees. Eventually, she was appointed to take over as the schoolteacher in Brierley following Nell Harcourt's departure for college.
